mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 640i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 6 Series 640i engine replacement typically costs £2,300-£3,500 for a used N55 unit, £3,500-£4,500 for a reconditioned engine, and £4,820-£5,500 for a fully rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit costs add approximately £800-£1,200 depending on your location and the specialist's labour rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N55 engine failure in a BMW 6 Series 640i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of N55 engine trouble in a 640i include: long cranking times or difficulty starting (often HPFP-related), rattling noise from the engine bay at startup (timing chain stretch), engine misfires or loss of power, excessive oil consumption or visible oil leaks from the valve cover or oil filter housing, and the check engine light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 640i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 6 Series 640i is otherwise in good condition, a replacement engine can extend its life by 80,000+ miles and retain strong value. With a typical 2014-2016 640i valued at £13,000-£22,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,820-£5,500 plus fitting represents a sound investment compared to the £8,000-£10,000 main dealer alternative.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 640i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 6 Series 640i engine replacements take 1-3 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 6 Series 640i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 6 Series 640i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier, and reconditioned engines often carry a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my BMW 6 Series 640i engine during replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - specialist suppliers can offer upgraded N55 variants with calibrated ECU maps for rebuilt engines. Upgrades may include enhanced timing chain components, updated PCV systems to address oil separator failures, and improved cooling system components.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 640i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 640i joined the F06/F12/F13 6 Series range at launch in 2011 as the entry-level petrol option, positioned below the V8-powered 650i. Throughout its production run, the 640i was powered exclusively by variants of BMW's N55 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six - one of the brand's most significant modern engine families.

milestones.description: N55B30A, 3.0L twin-scroll turbocharged straight-six petrol, 320hp, launched with F12 Convertible and F13 Coupé
N55B30A, F06 Gran Coupé joins the range with identical 320hp output
Facelift (LCI) updates across F06/F12/F13; N55B30O0 engine code introduced with Euro 6 emissions compliance
F06/F12/F13 production ends; 640i nameplate retired from UK 6 Series range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 6 Series 640i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 640i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The N55-powered BMW 6 Series 640i is a refined grand tourer, but its 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six is not without known weaknesses. Replacement demand for the 640i is dominated by the N55B30A (2011-2014) and N55B30O0 (2014-2018) variants, with high-pressure fuel pump failure, timing chain stretch, and oil leaks being the most frequent drivers of replacement decisions. Rebuilt BMW 6 Series 640i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 640i N55 Engine Suffers Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The HPFP is a critical component in the direct fuel injection system, delivering fuel at the necessary pressures. Over time, internal wear causes the pump to lose pressure, leading to long cranking times, engine misfires, loss of power, and even engine stalling. This is particularly common on early N55 production units.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early; restores normal fuel delivery

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing original failure points, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if other N55 issues present (timing chain wear, oil leaks, turbo wear)

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2015 BMW 6 Series 640i is valued between £11,000 and £22,000 depending on body style, mileage and condition. For vehicles worth £11,000-£15,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,820-£5,500 plus fitting is financially viable and represents good value when the car is otherwise in excellent condition. For cars at the lower end of the value spectrum (under £11,000), a used or reconditioned engine may be the more sensible choice.
problems.recommendation: If your 640i's HPFP fails and the rest of the engine is healthy, replacing just the pump is the most cost-effective solution (£500-£800 at a specialist). However, if your N55 is high-mileage (80,000+) and showing other symptoms - timing chain rattle, oil consumption, or turbo wear - a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components offers better long-term value and peace of mind.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the BMW 6 Series 640i N55 Engine Suffers Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Timing chain issues in some N55 engines are sometimes due to the plastic material used in their engineering, which cannot withstand the stresses of engine operation and leads to premature wear. Symptoms include rattling noise from the engine, check engine light activation, and engine misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing chain components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain failure has caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2014-2016 BMW 6 Series 640i valued at £13,000-£22,000, a specialist timing chain replacement at £1,200-£1,800 is a worthwhile investment if caught early. A full rebuilt engine at £4,820-£5,500 remains cost-effective relative to vehicle value, especially for cars worth £15,000+.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine bay at startup, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Early intervention with a chain and tensioner replacement (£1,200-£1,800 at a specialist) can prevent catastrophic engine failure. If the chain has already failed and damaged the engine, a rebuilt unit is the only sensible path forward.
